summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for evaluation of acute kidney injury with creatinine elevated to 4.0 from a baseline of 1.8. She reported mild lower extremity edema but was otherwise asymptomatic. Workup revealed no urinary tract infection or structural kidney abnormalities on ultrasound. Her kidney function improved with IV albumin, suggesting a component of pre-renal azotemia. The nephrology team noted possible tacrolimus-related thrombotic microangiopathy but deferred biopsy given comorbidities and clinical improvement. Her blood pressure was elevated during admission, prompting an increase in carvedilol from 25 mg to 37.5 mg twice daily. She remained on stable immunosuppression with tacrolimus, prednisone, and dapsone, with continuation of liver-directed therapies including lactulose and rifaximin. By discharge, her creatinine had improved to 2.5, and she was transitioned to oral hydration and nutritional support with Nepro. She was discharged home with follow-up arranged and instructions to monitor kidney function and blood pressure.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Adverse effect of antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs, initial encounter
